I'm able to reproduce the rendering artifacts with cube_ebu_colors_480px.mp4. They seem to occur because v4l2h26fdec intermittently sends non-dmabuf / system memory frames down the pipeline. This exposes a weakness in my
Keep previous QVideoFrameTextures alive until next frame is rendered
patch, where an incoming system memory texture causes the previous dmabuf texture to be freed prematurely. Thanks for pointing out how this is solved in qml6glsink, we'll look into it.
A clean way to check if you're getting dmabuf or system memory from the pipeline is to set QT_LOGGING_RULES=qt.multimedia.gstvideorenderer=true, which gives an output like

...
qt.multimedia.gstvideorenderer: QGstVideoRenderer::render
qt.multimedia.gstvideorenderer: m_capsMemoryFormat 0 bufferMemoryFormat 2
qt.multimedia.gstvideorenderer:     sending video frame
qt.multimedia.gstvideorenderer: QGstVideoRenderer::render
qt.multimedia.gstvideorenderer: m_capsMemoryFormat 0 bufferMemoryFormat 2
qt.multimedia.gstvideorenderer:     sending video frame
qt.multimedia.gstvideorenderer: QGstVideoRenderer::render
qt.multimedia.gstvideorenderer: m_capsMemoryFormat 0 bufferMemoryFormat 0
qt.multimedia.gstvideorenderer:     sending video frame
...
, where 0 is system memory, and 2 is dmabuf memory.
m_capsMemoryFormat is always 0, because  v4l2 elements don't necessarily advertise dmabuf in their caps, making it tricky to force them to send us dmabuf. It sounds like this is fixed in GSstreamer

We need to find a fix for earlier versions, and it would be nice to figure out what causes v4l2h264dec to choose system memory over dmabuf for certain frames. When I play cube_ebu_colors_480px.mp4, it happens a lot less frequent than in your videos. And when running without QT_MULTIMEDIA_FORCE_GL_TEXTURE_EXTERNAL_OES, the glitches are only visible as subtle lagging instead of the diagonal tearing artifacts. In either case I expect increased CPU usage related to handling these sporadic system memory buffers.

Great to hear that the video rendering is stable on your side as well. I would only recommend setting QT_MULTIMEDIA_FORCE_GL_TEXTURE_EXTERNAL_OES if things doesn't work without it. The gl_texture_external_oes approach was implemented before we realised it wasn't strictly needed. However for some devices it seems to improve performance drastically, e.g. on i.MX 8m mini. fields.summary: Wayland: Port tst_client to use new "shared" classes

issuetype.description: A task that needs to be done
issuetype.name: Task

customfield_10020.name: Wayland Project - Backlog task
customfield_10020.goal: Execute backlog tasks that have been discussed and agreed on

content.text: The tst_client test in Qt Wayland is the last one to use shared_old/ code, so once it is ported to use the replacements under shared/ all of that code can be deleted from the repository.
tst_client and shared_old folder are mostly testing wl_shell and etc in wayland.xml.
One example in other tests and shared folder, like tst_xdgshell, is testing xdg_wm_base and etc in xdg_shell.xml.
Should we port shared_old folder to new style like xdgshell.h/.cpp in shared folder?
Ah, most wl things are in coreprotocol.h/.cpp, continue reading.
https://github.com/qt/qtwayland/blob/dev/src/3rdparty/protocol/wayland.xml#L980-L981
Note! This protocol is deprecated and not intended for production use.
For desktop-style user interfaces, use xdg_shell.
Perhaps that's the reason why Johan didn't add classes for wl_shell and wl_shell_surface.
Then it looks like better to port tst_client to use xdg_wm_base and xdg_surface.

As long as we support wl_shell, we should keep the tests for it, in my opinion. But I agree that if porting that is a lot of work, then it doesn't make sense to do it just to support a deprecated protocol that hardly anyone uses. Do you think it would be a lot of work? Maybe it would be better to keep the test as it is until we remove wl_shell at some point in the future?

fields.summary: QtLocation maps to Qt 6.2

issuetype.description: A task that needs to be done
issuetype.name: Task

content.text: I have started to port QtLocation maps to Qt 6.2 and this issue is to track and collect all the relevant information.
Current status:
All classes are included into CMake build and modified for Qt 6.
OpenGL backend code of MapPolyline, MapPolygn, MapcCircle and MapRectangle (including labs project) is ported to new abstract graphics API.

MapboxGL plugin is re-introdced as MaplibreGL plugin. It compiles on MSVC, Android and iOS and is pointed to the official MapLibre repository because all needed changes are merged to main in MapLibre.
Bigger modifications:

Mouse and touch input part is re-written to support new 'exclusiveGrabber' and to be able to share different touch point between different child items. For example, one finger can pan the map and another finger can scroll child ListView.
Known issues:

Map tiles are not visible during flick animation. But they are when performing 'center' property CoordinateAnimation on the QML side. No idea, what's the cause. Flick movement is basically the same, only on the C++ side.
Fixed with
https://codereview.qt-project.org/c/qt/qtlocation/+/373996

MapPolyline extruded version has scrambled miter joints when route/polyline contains equal coordinates twice in the path, next to each other. Seems that routes can have this, when it contains multiple route segments or something.
But, the same behaviour is in Qt 5.
WIP: "mapboxgl" plugin has been switched to Maplibre. I compiles and works. TODO: rename everything an re-introduce it a "maplibregl" plugin.
Tests are not included.
https://codereview.qt-project.org/c/qt/qtlocation/+/380646/8
Examples are not yet ported/included.
Gestures: when panning the map with one finger to an offset and then placing a second finger on the map, then map jumps in a panned distance
. Fixed:
https://codereview.qt-project.org/c/qt/qtlocation/+/412441

-Gestures: holding down one finger until long press is triggered in child MouseArea, placing second finger on the map and releasing the first one, causes zoom gesture when moving the second (the only one left) - as if the first finger is still down-. Fixed:
https://codereview.qt-project.org/c/qt/qtlocation/+/412446

I'm not on Windows, so you might need to adjust the commands a bit. But in general here is what you need to do:
1. Clone the qtlocation repo and all the submodules into some directory:

git clone git://code.qt.io/qt/qtlocation.git
git submodule update --init --recursive
2. Create a directory for building QtLocation, and use qt-configure-module utility from Qt installation to configure the module properly

mkdir qtlocation_build
cd qtlocation_build
<path to Qt install dir>/bin/qt-configure-module.bat <path to your qtlocation sources>
3. Build the module and install it (call it in the same build directory)

cmake --build . --parallel
cmake --install .

I think you can also build the module in QtCreator. To do that, after executing step 2, just open the module's main CMakeLists.txt in QtCreator, and specify your qtlocation_build directory as a build directory while configuring.
P.S.: Of course you need to have git and CMake pre-installed for that.

Small note about iOS static build: linking OBJECT libraries is not too well supported on older CMake versions and I made a workaround by using BUILD_INTERFACE generator expression. But... it's  not reliable and you might end up with the error:

So, if you use CMake 3.21+ anyway then you might want to use
TARGET_OBJECTS
generator expression. In that case it doesn't require to export those dependent object libraries because they are bundled into the final lib file anyway.
Just apply the patch:

--- a/src/plugins/geoservices/maplibregl/CMakeLists.txt
+++ b/src/plugins/geoservices/maplibregl/CMakeLists.txt
@@ -41,11 +41,11 @@ qt_internal_add_plugin(QGeoServiceProviderFactoryMaplibreGLPlugin
         Qt::OpenGL
         Qt::Network
         Qt::LocationPrivate
-        "$<BUILD_INTERFACE:qmapboxgl>"
-        "$<BUILD_INTERFACE:mbgl-core>"
-        "$<BUILD_INTERFACE:mbgl-vendor-parsedate>"
-        "$<BUILD_INTERFACE:mbgl-vendor-nunicode>"
-        "$<BUILD_INTERFACE:mbgl-vendor-csscolorparser>"
+        "$<TARGET_OBJECTS:qmapboxgl>"
+        "$<TARGET_OBJECTS:mbgl-core>"
+        "$<TARGET_OBJECTS:mbgl-vendor-parsedate>"
+        "$<TARGET_OBJECTS:mbgl-vendor-nunicode>"
+        "$<TARGET_OBJECTS:mbgl-vendor-csscolorparser>"
 )
 
 qt_add_resources(plugin_resource_files maplibregl.qrc)
UPDATE

: Using TARGET_OBJETS is not a solution either. It doesn't seem to link all the objects into plugin lib file (although it should, as far as I understand). And having a second look at the doc, using BUILD_INTERFACE should be quite a correct solution to avoid install time dependencies and I'm 100% sure it used to work. Perhaps it's a bug in recent CMake versions or something. I have to spend more time on it.
UPDATE 2
: I finally found the cause. BUILD_INTERFACE evaluates to the expression also "when the property is exported using
export()
". And it seems that
export()
is added to the
qt_install
function in
QtInstallHelpers.cmake
. So I assume it's a change in Qt that introduced the problem.

Interesting use case; for now we are stripping Qt Location down to the basics; we have too many customization points in Qt 5, with dynamic parameters, extra parameters, additional parameters... those come all with a lot of code, complexity, and fragility.

The support for injecting additional map geometry and data to the backend engine through DynamicParameters was very incomplete, and only implemented for the mapbox backend. For now, it's gone. If we bring such backend-specific features back, then probably also through a backend specific API, rather than through something that looks cross-backend and then doesn't work for most of them.

With Qt 6.5 we are bringing Qt Location back. We start with the module as a technology preview, as we want to keep the option open to follow up on some of the API changes and additions.

The Qt 6 version is in many ways an improvement over Qt 5's Qt Location, but it is not fully feature-equivalent. If and when we bring some of the removed capabilities back - be it backends for additional providers, APIs for customizations, or functionality such as turn-by-turn navigation (which was only experimental in Qt 5 as well) - will depend on the feedback, use cases, and contributions. And it's not unlikely that a few bugs have slipped through.

I'm closing this ticket now, it has served its purpose, and we can manage new ideas and bugs reported in separate tickets. Thanks a lot to everyone participating and contributing, and in particular to
for kicking off the porting work, and for supporting the community on this channel! ❤️
Thank you! One epoch is finally over... let the new one start!

I have started to port QtLocation maps to Qt 6.2 and this issue is to track and collect all the relevant information.

Current status:
 * All classes are included into CMake build and modified for Qt 6. It builds!
 * OpenGL backend code of MapPolyline, MapPolygn, MapcCircle and MapRectangle is deleted. Software rendering (which is default) is available.
 * Labs project has no QSG implementations included (only interface classes) because they depended on the main MapPolyline, etc.
 * A few geoservices plugins (esri, nokia, itemsoverlay) are also not yet included.

Bigger modifications:
 * Mouse and touch input part is re-written to support new 'exclusiveGrabber' and to be able to share different touch point between different child items. For example, one finger can pan the map and another finger can scroll child ListView.

Known issues:
 * Map tiles are not visible during flick animation. But they are when performing 'center' property CoordinateAnimation on the QML side. No idea, what's the cause. Flick movement is basically the same, only on the C++ side.

 * MapboxGL plugin is re-introdced as MaplibreGL plugin. It compiles on MSVC, Android and iOS but is pointed to a fork of maplibre repository because it needs changes to be merged into the main repo.

 * Mouse and touch input part is re-written to support new 'exclusiveGrabber' and to be able to share different touch point between different child items. For example, one finger can pan the map and another finger can scroll child ListView.

* Gestures: when panning the map with one finger to an offset and then placing a second finger on the map, then map jumps in a panned distance.
* Gestures: holding down one finger until long press is triggered, placing second finger on the map and releasing the first one, causes zoom gesture when moving the second (the only one left) - as if the first finger is still down.
* There seems to be a change either in Qt 6.3 or in iOS where shaders don't have enouch precision. Moving GL objects (polyline, etc) are jumping when panning with bigger zoom levels. Even if _split double_ is used. This "jumping" goes away when using: QQuickWindow::setGraphicsApi(QSGRendererInterface::OpenGLRhi);

 * Mouse and touch input part is re-written to support new 'exclusiveGrabber' and to be able to share different touch point between different child items. For example, one finger can pan the map and another finger can scroll child ListView.

Known issues:
 * -Map tiles are not visible during flick animation. But they are when performing 'center' property CoordinateAnimation on the QML side. No idea, what's the cause. Flick movement is basically the same, only on the C++ side.- Fixed with [https://codereview.qt-project.org/c/qt/qtlocation/+/373996]
 * -MapPolyline extruded version has scrambled miter joints when route/polyline contains equal coordinates twice in the path, next to each other. Seems that routes can have this, when it contains multiple route segments or something.- But, the same behaviour is in Qt 5.
 * -WIP: "mapboxgl" plugin has been switched to Maplibre. I compiles and works. TODO: rename everything an re-introduce it a "maplibregl" plugin.-
 * -Tests are not included.- [https://codereview.qt-project.org/c/qt/qtlocation/+/380646/8]
 * Examples are not yet ported/included.
 * -Gestures: when panning the map with one finger to an offset and then placing a second finger on the map, then map jumps in a panned distance-. Fixed: https://codereview.qt-project.org/c/qt/qtlocation/+/412441
 * Gestures: holding down one finger until long press is triggered, placing second finger on the map and releasing the first one, causes zoom gesture when moving the second (the only one left) - as if the first finger is still down.
 * There seems to be a change either in Qt 6.3 or in iOS where shaders don't have enouch precision. Moving GL objects (polyline, etc) are jumping when panning with bigger zoom levels. Even if _split double_ is used. This "jumping" goes away when using: _QQuickWindow::setGraphicsApi(QSGRendererInterface::OpenGLRhi);_. It happens only on iOS (perhaps Mac as well) and default RHI (Metal, I guess). Android and Windows are smooth.

fields.summary: Consider reintroducing Linux support with NearD

issuetype.description: A user story for the product
issuetype.name: User Story

content.text: Linux support was dropped when migrating to Qt 6.
Now when a new 0.17 release of NearD [0] is out, we can consider reimplementing support for it.
https://github.com/linux-nfc/neard

Are there any examples of readers/writers supported by neard? It does not seem to support an obvious way of using smartcards (NRC or not) on Linux - using an USB CCID device. The neard's documentation does not help at all. From what I can see it only supports integrated devices that are represented as /dev/nfc? by the Linux kernel. I am yet to see such devices in the wild.
Is there a reason why we limit ourselves to NFC? Do we currently have any features that are not usable with other smart cards?
We have 5.15 implementation at
https://github.com/qt/qtconnectivity/tree/5.15/src/nfc/neard
, so it should be much easier to port to Qt 6, I assume.
See also
https://elinux.org/images/d/d1/Near_Field_Communication_with_Linux.pdf

I will have a go at bringing back neard support in QtNFC / Qt6 by bringing back and fixing up the Qt5 code. It's for an embedded platform that has NFC hardware connected via i²c. Of course you don't see that on PC-type platforms. But it exists.

I am not sure if it will result in something of upstreamable quality because the neard used on the system in question is actually a (hopefully) protocol-compatible reimplementation due to differences in the stack below. The system in question also supports NFC via i²c via Ethernet, which happens to be much easier to add to the open source but hardware-specific NXP stack, which has much more of the protocol handling in user space. On top of that sits the alternative neard which only works with the NXP stack.
So neard support won't be tested with the actual neard without additional effort that my customer may or may not want to support.

A question about bringing back the old backend: any idea about how to choose the backend at runtime (or compile time - I'm not sure)? AFAIU, it used to be that there was exactly one backend per platform, so a backend selection mechanism has never been required so far. This is with upstreaming in mind of course - a proprietary hack can easily hardcode it.

any idea about how to choose the backend at runtime (or compile time - I'm not sure)? AFAIU, it used to be that there was exactly one backend per platform, so a backend selection mechanism has never been required so far.

Compile-time backend selection is already implemented in Qt NFC. It's just about including the proper files based on the detected platform/OS. We have at least Android, iOS, and PCSC backends as of now.
Runtime backend selection is used, for example, in Qt Positioning. You can have a look at the implementation of
QGeoPositionInfoSource::createSource()
for inspiration.
In Qt NFC, you might probably want to have something similar for
QNearFieldManager
OK, thanks! (To clarify, I meant compile time selection based on something other than
just
the current platform, like the availability of a dependency or a flag or a combination. But, I guess it's more or less standard CMake, with which I have some experience.)
See:
https://codereview.qt-project.org/c/qt/qtconnectivity/+/522967
(last commit in a chain of commits to restore neard support, there is also a topic for it)
I'm not sure who to ask to review this. How it is organized into commits is also up for review.
I had only a brief look at the patch chain. I'd suggest that you add
Task-number: QTBUG-97943
to the footer of every commit message (just before the Change-Id footer). This way all patches will be visible in this Jira ticket.
I've added the Task-number footer
So, how to proceed? qtconnectivity doesn't seem to be very maintained and this patch series contains relatively large changes that need someone to approve them eventually.
Unfortunately, this patch chain would not make it into 6.7, because the Feature Freeze is in the end of this week, so we would not have time to reasonably review and test the changes.
But I'm personally willing to review it and make it available for Qt 6.8. And I do know some other people who might help us with the reviews.
However, one big question here is that last time we had a look at it, we were not able to find any hardware that works with NearD, at least on Linux Desktop.

do you have some actual hardware examples that can be used to test your patch chain? You were talking about embedded devices earlier, but probably there is something for Desktop as well? Or at least some reasonable embedded devices that we could get for testing?
Thanks for the reply and your willingness to help. I will look for, preferably USB, hardware options compatible with neard.

I think ACR122U devices might be an option. They contain a sort of hardware wrapper around the recommended for Linux NXP PN532 chip as per Linux kernel commit 53cf48399ad3b08c9115b4fce73dee0b6e726c91 from 2013, which adds support. That support is even in the actual PN532 driver. Devices are available at reasonable prices:
https://www.reichelt.de/nfc-cardreader-usb-plusonic-195630-p302801.html
https://de.aliexpress.com/item/1005005213152787.html
Does anyone have more information about this device, especially concerning neard?
I have ordered an ACR122U device and will check if that does anything useful.
Hi
Did you manage to test the ACR122U device? Does it work with neard?

I have the device, tested it, and it doesn't work. The kernel driver apparently works fine, and the device beeps when holding a MIFARE tag next to it,  but next to nothing seems to happen in neard. The device reportedly works in a libusb based stack, but I don't really care about that. That variant doesn't even use the kernel driver.
I've also got the hardware and can try it and see if something can be done there.
For now I can confirm that ACR122U works with pcsclite but does not work with the current neard patch.

I've managed to read type 4 tags with some changes to the branch (see my comments on Gerrit). However I'm not entirely happy with the branch organization. In particular, I'm not happy that intermediate commits are not buildable. I understand that this is a revert, but given that I'm not familiar with the original code, this organization makes the patchset hard to review. Maybe it is better to squash everything that is not an unrelated change together and review the patch as a new frontend? Code modernization can be added on top.
Very cool, thanks!! I thought it was a harder to fix problem in lower layers.

I understand the concern about not buildable commits. I wanted to keep the revert and additional work separate, but revert + build (+ very obvious functionality - not including the "Dual" one in that) fixes in a single commit is okay for me, too.
: I ended up squashing all of your patches except one together, otherwise it was not possible to compile patches in CI. The patchset compiles now fine and works for me.
A change related to this issue (sha1 'cb9d34f2a9a5c6c66c6fe9eb6628eb7627f3bb04')  was integrated in 'qt/qtconnectivity' in the 'dev' branch.

fields.summary: PCSCLite/winscard support in QtNfc

issuetype.description: A user story for the product
issuetype.name: User Story

content.text: Currently we have NFC module that seems to be only useful for reading smartcards, but cannot be used with USB-connected devices on desktop platforms. It would be good to support smartcard readers on desktop platforms too. Perhaps using pcsclite on Unix-like systems. PCSClite API is based on Windows PCSC API (
https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winscard/
It may be possible to use the same API as used for NFC, it will be misnamed then.
Note that neard support (
) seems much less usable on Linux, unless I'm missing something.
PCSC is used by Qt-based AusweisApp, the code there does seem to support Windows too.
macOS was using a fork of PCSCLite in the past for smart card access, that is not the case anymore. CryptoTokenKit is the API to use on macOS.
https://www.ausweisapp.bund.de/en/ausweisapp2-home/
, yes that's AusweisApp I'm referring to in the issue description.
The AusweisApp supports PCSC on Linux, BSD, macOS and Windows:
https://github.com/Governikus/AusweisApp2/tree/master/src/card/pcsc
Feel free to ask for help.

: The plan is to have something that would be useful for apps like AusweisApp and also compatible with the API we have in Qt. I'll certainly include you in the review when patches are somewhat usable. Unfortunately it is not quite simple to use pcsclite/scard API with Qt event loop, as you've probably already discovered.
I've split CryptoTokenKit to
: I like the extension of the NFC module to work on desktop system too. But with the current interface we will probably not be able to use it in the AusweisApp2.
On mobile systems all works fine, because we only have one "reader" there. So all we need is a QNearFieldTarget.
On desktop systems we have multiple reader, that could also have a PIN pad.
To support the user in the GUI we need also information about the connected reader without a card.
These information is the name used by PCSC and the
readerFeatures
for the PIN pad.
The product and vendor ID would also be great but is not mandatory.
Edit: Looks like
can be the solution
: Thanks for the feedback. I hope that the QtNfc interface could be improved to satisfy those requirements. I've added your comments to
for now.

content.text: The format is described here:
https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/
There is already an implementation of protobuf generator for Qt here:
https://github.com/semlanik/qtprotobuf
, it is done bu
. It also includes client-side support for GRPC. The current license is MIT, so compatible with Qt.
As far as I can see, the project provides tools for generating code from proto files, and 2 libraries to support protobuf and gRPC usage (see also
) that need to be linked into applications, there is also CMake code to help to integrate everything into application.
There are some things that need to be done before this can be integrated in Qt, but that doable:
CMake usage need to be updated to current standards
Changes needed to how QtNetwork API is used
Qt6 need to be supported
Additionally tests and examples need to be update. Documentation need to be integrated into the rest of Qt documentation.
Should this be integrated in some existing module or should it become a new module?
Here is simplified design just to give the representation of relations between existing
https://github.com/semlanik/qtprotobuf
components and the 3rdparties
IIUC the serialization (plugin) support in there is to read in/out formats which are not protobuf? I see JSON in there.
Also, it requires 'go', is it just for parsemessages.go (ignoring the usage in the example)?
Looked at this module for a little bit, questions above.
Updated to make it compile with Qt 6. Surprisingly it uses 20GB of RAM or so to compile the project? Some issues with namespaces. Metatype got an update for Qt6 so a lot of tests are failing.
Sorry, I missed comments.
> IUC the serialization (plugin) support.
This might not be required, but yeah this is to replace or add new serializers of the same type.
> Also, it requires 'go', is it just for parsemessages.go (ignoring the usage in the example)?
Go is not required anymore, I replaced the script yesterday.
> Updated to make it compile with Qt 6. Surprisingly it uses 20GB of RAM or so to compile the project? Some issues with namespaces. Metatype got an update for Qt6 so a lot of tests are failing.
I also started the porting to Qt6. If no one is doing the same currently, I can spend some time(personal) to complete it till the end of this week.
I did some stuff on our gitlab instance (
https://git.qt.io/manordhe/qtprotobuf)
, though I haven't changed anything beyond what was needed to make it compile with Qt6 and fixing (some?) deprecation warnings. + made it compile with a namespaced build of Qt.

I have to admit that putting huge amount of generated proto messages into a single .cpp file not a such good idea. But I don't observe the same amount of memory eaten when compiling against Qt5.

Faced this as well. Checking how to fix the "basic" protobuf types.
> But I don't observe the same amount of memory eaten when compiling against Qt5.

It might also be an MSVC thing, each of the generated files used about 700MB to compile + an extra process for storing the debug information using 300MB. I was running with many threads so it quickly used a lot of memory

ported to Qt6 using qt_internal_ API's. I also fixed some issue I faced and suppressed the check of QMetaProperty.typeName(),  need to spend more efforts to check how the fresh metatype system names the property types. QML support is pending. I will switch to our gitlab instance tomorrow evening.
Will try to complete migration from gtest to QtTest tomorrow and understand how to deal with QML.

I almost complete porting. Documentation, features and few points I marked by "TODO Qt6" are left. Also I reduced the consumption of memory by decomposing the tests. Will continue tomorrow, hope it's ok. Also need to update licenses, but here I definitely need someones help.
PS: Updates are on gilab

Ah, sweet. Yeah, I can likely help with the licensing stuff. Will take a look at the MR in an hour or so, and probably just give you direct push rights.

The format is described here: https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/

There is already an implementation of protobuf generator for Qt here: https://github.com/semlanik/qtprotobuf , it is done bu [~accountid:712020:b808bfaf-2522-4ba6-8d19-2011a4ac108b]. It also includes support for GRPC. The current license is MIT, so compatible with Qt.

As far as I can see, the project provides tools for generating code from proto files, and 2 libraries to support protobuf and GPRC usage that need to be linked into applications, there is also CMake code to help to integrate everything into application.

There are some things that need to be done before this can be integrated in Qt, but that doable:
* GRPS support is in need of refactoring (there is no client-side subscription support for example).
* CMake usage need to be updated to current standards
* Changes needed to how QtNetwork API is used
* Qt6 need to be supported

Additionally tests and examples need to be update. Documentation need to be integrated into the rest of Qt documentation.

There is already an implementation of protobuf generator for Qt here: https://github.com/semlanik/qtprotobuf , it is done bu [~accountid:712020:b808bfaf-2522-4ba6-8d19-2011a4ac108b]. It also includes support for GRPC. The current license is MIT, so compatible with Qt.

As far as I can see, the project provides tools for generating code from proto files, and 2 libraries to support protobuf and GPRC usage that need to be linked into applications, there is also CMake code to help to integrate everything into application.

There are some things that need to be done before this can be integrated in Qt, but that doable:
* GRPS support is in need of refactoring (there is no client-side subscription support for example).
* Server-side GPRC support is missing (simplechatserver example is using the reference GRPC implementation).
* CMake usage need to be updated to current standards
* Changes needed to how QtNetwork API is used
* Qt6 need to be supported

Additionally tests and examples need to be update. Documentation need to be integrated into the rest of Qt documentation.

content.text: Overview:
Android 11 (API level 30) further enhances the platform, giving better protection to app and user data on external storage.
This release introduces several enhancements, such as raw file path access, batch edit operations for media, and an updated UI for the Storage Access Framework.
Changes:

On Android 11, apps with the read external storage permission are able to access files with file paths in the scoped storage environment. On Android 10 devices, this is not available to apps in the scoped storage environment unless they have opted out by setting the android:requestLegacyExternalStorage manifest attribute.
Android 11 allows you to use APIs other than the
MediaStore
API to access media files from shared storage using
direct file paths
. These APIs include the following:
The
File
API.
Native libraries, such as fopen().
Proposed Actions:
Check if Qt Android accesses files with filepaths outside
Check our usage of MediaStore API. Do we save or load resources using MediaStore? Should we?
How we proccess file system URI´s (content uris, direct file, etc)
Follow this:
https://developer.android.com/training/data-storage/use-cases#access-file-paths
Check android manifest flags and API target.
Related to
Ping, please find and list here the related Jira items
https://forum.qt.io/topic/136090/using-qdesktopservices-with-android-11-scoped-storage
Relates to
Related to
No time yet
Touched on the QDesktopServices::openUrl() and the ongoing work to add FileProvider to access scoped file paths.

https://github.com/KDAB/android/tree/master/shared_storage
example use:

Solution in C++:
And add in manifest file:
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE"/>
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE" />
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE"/>
using ACTION_MANAGE_APP_ALL_FILES_ACCESS_PERMISSION would require MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE which is not intended for every app, not every app will be allowed to use that permission, check
https://developer.android.com/reference/android/Manifest.permission#MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE
Thanks for the links they are helpful, I'm working on adding support for similar operations under scoped storage for Qt.
In progress to add the missing scoped storage facilities to deal with content urls under AndroidContentFileEngine implementation, atm I'm preparing a full patch before pushing to gerrit.

mentioned in the comment, because the app is a DropBox-like app to manage files from shared network drives or SharePoints.

QStandardPathes still gives no access to files

KDAB SharedStorage Library
mentioned in the comments.

Selecting a folder and then
creating a file inside the folder works great.
Then I found out, that
QDir and QFile not only support file pathes, but also Content URIs
This seems not to be documented yet, because full ScopedStorage support not ready yet (
https://qt-project.atlassian.net/browse/QTBUG-99664
But the current implementation helps if using the
QML FileDialog on Android

QML FileDialog

W libenbwDOCS_x_arm64-v8a.so: qrc:/android_rcc_bundle/qml/QtQuick/Controls/Styles/Android/LabelStyle.qml:94: TypeError: Cannot read property 'ENABLED_SELECTED_STATE_SET' of undefined

Hello! I have a question about the patch, is there a reason for creating a cpp implementation of `DocumentFile` and going down this route?

In my implementation of scoped storage in Qt, I remember having to deal with very finicky things like weird undocumented encoding rules, treeUri -> documentTreeUri and back etc and more importantly caching (DocumentsContract API is very slow especially if you do directory operations).
and “Unknown error” from QFile, per ex. using "content://com.android.externalstorage.documents/tree/primary%3ADocuments/ekke.txt"

This is probably happening because you're trying to open file descriptor on  a treeUri, you have to have a document uri version of tree uri (I forgot what it was called officially, I just call it documentTreeUri). Something that looks like:
content://com.android.externalstorage.documents/tree/primary%3Atencent/document/primary%3Atencent%2Ffilename.txt
Thanks for testing and the notes.
selecting files only selects one file
– haven’t found a way to select multiple files using KDABs SharedStorage library and this is essential for users.

creating a file inside the folder works great.
That's because EXTRA_ALLOW_MULTIPLE is not passed as an extra to the intent of the file dialog, while Qt side pass that.
Then I found out, that QDir and QFile not only support file pathes, but also Content URIs.
This seems not to be documented yet, because full ScopedStorage support not ready yet (
https://qt-project.atlassian.net/browse/QTBUG-99664
But the current implementation helps if using the QML FileDialog on Android
Yes, there's some support for content URI in the current Qt Apis, however, it's still missing some features, which this ticket tries to cover.
Create File in folder: I can select a folder, was asked for permission, but then trying to create a file inside the selected folder, I’m getting errors:
E Qt JAVA : openFdForContentUrl(): No permissions to open Uri
and “Unknown error” from QFile, per ex. using "content://com.android.externalstorage.documents/tree/primary%3ADocuments/ekke.txt"

This is one of the operations that the current Qt Apis don't support, I have it working locally with QFile though, but it's still not in a shape I'm fully happy with. But this would be a fix that we need to get into Qt APIs though.

Hello! I have a question about the patch, is there a reason for creating a cpp implementation of `DocumentFile` and going down this route?

In my implementation of scoped storage in Qt, I remember having to deal with very finicky things like weird undocumented encoding rules, treeUri -> documentTreeUri and back etc and more importantly caching...

Indeed, the encoding is a bit messy dealing with content Uris, the Android APIs seem to return partially encoded paths, mainly the documentId part is encoded, and using a wrong encoding might not work.
The use of DocumentFile is just an abstraction, DocumentContracts is used under the hood.
(DocumentsContract API is very slow especially if you do directory operations)

But I meant it in the context of comparing it to simple Unix file – where caching is not something you have to think of, with DocumentsContract the performance is pretty poor, especially if calls are made on fly to ContentResolver (which does IPC, permissions check etc behind the scenes). That's why I mentioned that caching is something which should be thought of beforehand and for that, I believe keeping things on Java is simpler, because otherwise there would be a burden to main the JNI interface for caching as well. I hope I am clear this time
Also, it would be helpful to mention what alternatives to use instead that you've dealt with this in some shape before?

I think it is possible to have that in 5.15, but for now I'll update the patch to have it on dev and add few more changes on top, then once we have it in dev and everything works as expected, we can worry about 5.15 because it will have some merge conflicts for sure.

https://github.com/android/storage-samples/blob/master/ActionOpenDocumentTree/app/src/main/java/com/example/android/ktfiles/CachingDocumentFile.kt

h2. Overview:

Android 11 (API level 30) further enhances the platform, giving better protection to app and user data on external storage.

This release introduces several enhancements, such as raw file path access, batch edit operations for media, and an updated UI for the Storage Access Framework.
h2. Changes:

On Android 11, apps with the read external storage permission are able to access files with file paths in the scoped storage environment. On Android 10 devices, this is not available to apps in the scoped storage environment unless they have opted out by setting the android:requestLegacyExternalStorage manifest attribute.

Android 11 allows you to use APIs other than the [MediaStore|https://developer.android.com/reference/android/provider/MediaStore] API to access media files from shared storage using [direct file paths|https://developer.android.com/training/data-storage/shared/media#direct-file-paths]. These APIs include the following:
 * The [File|https://developer.android.com/reference/java/io/File] API.
 * Native libraries, such as fopen().

h2. Proposed Actions:
 * Check if Qt Android accesses files with filepaths outside
 * Check our usage of MediaStore API. Do we save or load resources using MediaStore? Should we?
 * How we proccess file system URI´s (content uris, direct file, etc)
 * Follow this: [https://developer.android.com/training/data-storage/use-cases#access-file-paths]
 * Check android manifest flags and API target.

content.text: Currently, the installer is build for x86 only. Thanks to Rosetta translation layer, x86 binaries can be run on M1 Macs as well. However, when Apple stops supporting Rosetta, we need to have ARM builds for Installer and IFW as well.
As a consequence, Qt 5.15.x versions, on which installer/IFW are based, must be built for Mac/ARM as well.
will check, whether this is actually needed.

Currently, we build only x86 packages for the installer. This means we still use Rosetta layer. Packaging is preparing x86/ARM binaries though, so this will be fixed in the near future. After the packages are available, this will be closed.
After these are in
https://codereview.qt-project.org/q/project:qt/tqtc-qt5+branch:tqtc/lts-ifw-5.15.8+status:open
I can do the required instruction changes to master to be merged to tqtc/master.
I am very much looking forward to having native arm64 qtifw installers.

I have an M1 max MBP. I build a (large) C++ project and package with qtifw. I noticed it was significantly slower than I was used too, binarycreator was the bottleneck and taking at most 4 threads (due to Rosetta probably), when installed from the Qt installer (this is an x86 program currently).
I built a static qt5 from the git sources manually today, then built qtinstaller-framework from source as a native app. (I had to patch one file in qt5 due to a missing import).
The result is that the x86 takes 10minutes and the arm64 one takes 2.5 minutes, so a 4x speedup (I could see the native one use all the available threads on my machine)
x86 QtIFW installers, producing the package (IFW and Tar gz)
real    10m17.444s
user    9m30.974s
sys     0m28.038s
Same, with custom QtIFW (4.4.0) with a static qt 5.15, native arm64
real	2m50.321s
user	6m51.565s
sys	0m28.321s
Did you try if one can get same benefit by using universal binary? The current plan is still to create one installer, but universal binary which would work without Rosetta.
Is there a universal binary I could download to try and time? Otherwise how do I produce it? What I've done so far is to basically follow
https://doc.qt.io/qtinstallerframework/ifw-getting-started.html
except I also passed `QMAKE_APPLE_DEVICE_ARCHS=arm64` to qmake.
I couldn't figure how to create a .dmg installer from that (which I suppose involves using QtIFW to package this QtIFW installer. I tried to reproduce some of the steps in
https://github.com/qtproject/installer-framework/blob/master/tools/build_installer.py
but It didn't work)
Unfortunately not yet available, but it is just amending the 'armv64' with x86_64: "QMAKE_APPLE_DEVICE_ARCHS=x86_64 arm64"
Hum, isn't that only possible on x86 macs? x86 should be able to cross compile to arm64, the other way isn't possible if I recall correctly.
Enablers in CI has been  in place for some time now. But there is now another issue:
https://qt-project.atlassian.net/browse/QTIFW-2750
Is there any progress on this, a year later? Thanks!

fields.summary: Research profiler support on Windows

issuetype.description: A technical task
issuetype.name: Technical task

content.text: Qt Creator's
manual page about profiling
mentions
callgrind
for analyzing / profiling an application. Callgrind is not available on Windows.
At
Profiling and Memory Checking Tools
we have multiple suggestions on how to deal with the matter on Windows.
The most promising is
Very Sleepy
which could handle both MSVC and MinGW.
It supports any native Windows app, if it has standard PDB or DWARF debugging information. No recompilation is necessary – it can just attach to any app as it's running.
Both 32-bit x86 and 64-bit x64 systems are fully supported, and Very Sleepy will work with both Visual Studio or gcc/mingw compilers.
Profiling results are displayed in full call-graph format, and can additionally be saved and exported to CSV format.
Later edit: Other candidates are:
google/orbit: C/C++ Performance Profiler (github.com)
wolfpld/tracy: Frame profiler (github.com)
Godot just added tracy to the engine and now to their scripting language GDScript
But I guess this would be more of a QtCore/QtQuick addition and only the view part should be done in QtCreator

https://developer.android.com/about/versions/13/features#color-vector-fonts
Android 13 adds rendering support for COLR version 1 (COLRv1) fonts and updates system emoji to the COLRv1 format.
Note:
However, if your app implements its own text rendering and uses the system's fonts, we recommend testing emoji rendering

Test emoji fonts on Android 13 and loading a COLR version font.
AFAIK, we use the system fonts with our rendering.
We need to test it and verify that emojis are still appropriately rendered; otherwise, it's a bug, IMHO.
what do you think?

Loaded emoji font from
https://github.com/googlefonts/color-fonts/tree/main/fonts

In previous Android versions, the COLRV1 fonts were loaded successfully as well but could not be rendered. This is expected as the support for rendering was introduced in Android 13.

fields.summary: Spike Automatically generate C++ and/or QML exposing Android Manager

issuetype.description: A task that needs to be done
issuetype.name: Task

content.text: Who
For Qt for Android developers at Qt and Community/Customers who use JNI
What
Android has many services/managers (e.g. TelephonyManager, PowerManager, WindowManager,...)
This task is about studying if it's possible to create some tools/scripts/... that can create the required code to expose those Android APIs to the C++ and/or QML.
Maybe create the required JNI code layers automatically...
Ultimately, if the above is not possible, we could aim to make it easier and trouble free to write Java code and invoke it from C++ so that developers can seamlessly write both codes.
Why
Speed up the development of new features at Qt
Community/customers to generate the required bindings for the Android and hopefully for their own services
When
Spike Q2-Q3/2022
Dependencies
Time (that's why P1)it's time-critical to know for a customer case if it's even feasible
Definition of Done
The expected outcome would be stories or tasks about a potential solution based on PoC (Proof of Concept) e.g. some kinda demo to increase awarenes
Start from easiest manager, develop automatized PoC
Results:
Initial Research:
First I searched for libs that would generate JNI code from Java. There are not many, but I found 3:
https://github.com/cowwoc/jace
Jace is several command-line tools that take java source files as a argument and generate JNI code from it.
It is more focused on types than classes and generic Java code. No examples with Android. The generator is quite old, made in 2012 and it does not generate code C++ 14.
No recent new updates on code since 8/10 years, project seems dead (just updates on documentation).
https://codemesh.com/index.php
A proprietary solution made to connect Java and C++ libraries.
Looks decent, but it looks too complex for our needs. From the website :

A code generator is used to analyze Java bytecode and generate C++ types that can be used just like the underlying Java types. A runtime library is responsible for setting up and maintaining the connection between the two sides when you run your application.

No idea if that would even work on Android since Java and Dalvik bytecode is different. The goal of this solution is for developers to create Java libs and integrate them with old C++ programs. It is the opposite different direction that we want. And having a runtime library in Android to connect both ends when we just need the JNI glue seems an overkill.
https://github.com/LanderlYoung/Jenny
An annotation processor for creating C++ and JNI code. Has examples with Android. Can use kotlin as well as Java.

It has 2 components: the Glue and the Proxy. The Glue is for creating native functions in C++ from Java, which is not very interesting, but the proxy is to create the JNI methods to call Java/Kotlin functions in C++. That is exactly what we need.
It generates the code at compile-time, which may open use cases outside of retrieving the managers from Android. This library is open-source (Apache 2.0 licensed), and it generates okay code.
The latest update was in Jun 2021. It does not look actively developed but it is in a good state. Also, it is published on maven-central.
Testing:
The most promising library was Jenny, so I made a small test with it.
It looks very promising! It can definitely be used as a tool for generating the JNI code.
I could use it in Qt Creator, there was no need for running Android Studio. Maybe a Qt Creator plugin in the future?
Easy to use. I used the maven one, so I did not even need to build the lib, just add it as a dependency in gradle. I used kotlin, but there is java version as well.
Generates the proxy C++ code for the Android Managers, and they are typed. Requires some configuration, but not too much.
Added my demo on this issue.
Points to improve:
C++ code generation on Jenny - currently text strings merged together.
Integration with Qt - Jenny and Qt do same thing in many places - Ex. Jni Object memory management, toString, fromString functions.
Proposed Next Steps:
How to integrate generated code with Qt. Possible solutions:
Change Jenny to use Qt functions
Create a wrapper around Jenny for interacting with Qt
Others (open to possibilities)
Improving Jenny
In near future - as a tool, which is the best way to provide this?
Scripts
Qt Creator plugin
Qt Desktop Application
Others (open to possibilities)
In the long run - Research feasibility and interest as a code generation step in Qt like in a moc for JNI.

fields.summary: qUncompress(qCompress()) round-trip fails for data > 2GiB

issuetype.description: A task that needs to be done
issuetype.name: Task

content.text: The code fails on 64-bit platforms:
It seems to be caused by qCompress() using only four digits to encode the length.
There doesn't appear to be something you can do, unless you change the format to include a longer length indicator.
I'll add code that rejects data > 4GiB to qCompress()

Any idea how to allow for more than 4GiB of data? Some fancy format change? Lie? qUncompress looks like it should be able to uncompress to more than the indicated length. In fact, I'm not sure why it fails.
I'd simply not fix this at all. Document as limitation and be done with it.
Use libzstd for more than 4 GB of data.
Actually, it
does
work. The reason why my test failed appears to have been
https://codereview.qt-project.org/c/qt/qtbase/+/421908

If the format isn't documented, we could write 0xffff'ffff into the header if the size is greater than that (instead of the current size mod UINT_MAX), to give a better guesstimate for qUncompress to start from on 64-bit, and for an early failure for qUncompress on 32-bit platforms. Or we refuse to accept more than 2GiB in qCompress().
Refusing to accept more than 2GiB in qCompress() would be a breaking change, as it currently works. So the question is what we should use as a length field in that case.
If we currently qCompress() UINT_MAX + 1 bytes on 64-bit, the length written will be 0x1, which means
::uncompress
will return
Z_BUF_ERROR

32 times until we've realloced to 8GiB. Maybe we should divide sizes > 4GiB by two until the result is < 4GiB and store that + 1 as the length field, so we end up with the correct (minimal) size after the minimum number of allocation doublings.
Or we always store 0xffff'ffff, to fail fast on 32-bit.
any opinion?
Refusing to accept more than 2GiB in qCompress() would be a breaking change, as it currently works.

By some definition of "works". It compresses, but it can't decompress what it produced, so I don't think we should honestly call that "works". I suppose someone has some code to work around the limitation, for example by not using
qUncompress()
and ignoring the 4-byte length and just trying an ever-increasing buffer size until zlib works. Or using zlib's streaming API, which they honestly should for any large decompression.
I am of the opinion we don't need to fix
qCompress()
and
qUncompress()
for large sizes.
As an example, take this tarball of Qt 6.3.0 and Qt Creator 8.0.0, which is just under 4 GB:
-rw-r--r--  1 tjmaciei tjmaciei 4053258240 Sep  6 14:07 qt-and-qt-creator.tar
This is how big the compression results are and how long they take to decompress:
Compression scheme
File size
Time to decompress (s)
RAM to decompress (kB)
zlib (default)
N/A
zlib level 9
N/A
Zstd level 19
Zstd level 22 long
Xz 9 extreme

Times measured on an otherwise idle Core i9-7940X (3.1 GHz); when measured on a Xeon Platinum 8260L @ 2.4 GHz, zstd and xz were ~20% slower and zlib was 50% slower (but also different Linux distros). Files were on a tmpfs, so I/O is not relevant. I couldn't easily measure the delta in RSS for
zcat
(the result was negative), so assume the RAM needed for zlib decompression is negligible.

That is apparently the only thing zlib is currently good at: negligible RAM overhead for decompression. Otherwise, it produces the biggest compressed output, even at its best compression level, and loses to Zstandard in decompression throughput. Considering the application that is trying to decompress must be allocating 4GB in RAM, the extra 8.4 MB is a rounding error.
Therefore, I argue it's not worth fixing this pair of functions for large data sets.
People should be using Zstandard
as a compression and they should also be protecting against compression bombs.
It compresses, but it can't decompress what it produced,
What do you mean? qUncompress() uses the length field only as a first allocation size (
https://github.com/qt/qtbase/blob/e0eb93d9a2b104ac8d7596c419d1f13dc9db9b1b/src/corelib/text/qbytearray.cpp#L609
). If uncompress() returns Z_BUF_ERROR, qUncompress() doubles the allocation (
https://github.com/qt/qtbase/blob/e0eb93d9a2b104ac8d7596c419d1f13dc9db9b1b/src/corelib/text/qbytearray.cpp#L640
) until either Z_OK is returned or we run into QByteArray size limitations.
So, even if the length field is wrong, we'll eventually succeed (as long as the result fits in principle into QByteArray size limitations).
Ahh... uLong is unsigned long, so only 32 bits. I see.
Ahh... uLong is unsigned long, so only 32 bits. I see.
On Windows. On 64-bit Unix (LP64), it's 64-bit.
Current understanding of the problem:
On 32-bit platforms, we can compress as much as available memory allows.
On 64-bit platforms where
sizeof(long) == 8
(everything except Windows), we can compress as much as available memory allows
but we cannot give a correct decompression-size hint, because, historically, that field is 32-bit wide

it's just a hint, though, so we don't need it to be exact. In fact, we can play tricks like putting an FP value there, as long as the MSB is set (so 32-bit platforms reject it outright) and, ideally, the value of the field interpreted as an unsigned BE integer is ≤ the real value
On 64-bit Windows,
sizeof(long) == 4
, so we're limited to 4GiB by zlib's use of
uLong
as the size type.
This appears to be fixable by using the zlib stream interface (
zstream
deflate()
inflate()
) directly instead of the convenience functions
compress2()
and
uncompress()
I'll create follow-up tasks to separate these two things. When the patch train referencing this Jira task is integrated, we have a consistent, documented state, at least, and we can work from there.
Actually, it fails for above 2 GB too, because:
qUncompress

size_t expectedSize = size_t((data[0] << 24) | (data[1] << 16) |
                                 (data[2] <<  8) | (data[3]      ));
has a bug.
is
int
because of integer promotion, so any value with the sign bit set is, therefore, negative. The cast to
size_t
doesn't fix it: we get sign extension.
For sizes between 4 and 6 GB, it'll work again. This is a test made by concatenating the tarballs of Qt 6.3.2 and GCC 12.2.0:

items.fromString:
Let's be honest: the change from int to qsizetype sizes in Qt 6.0 was more than rushed. Half the API and a good chunk of implementation code is still using int when it should be using qsizetype, and we have been papering over this issue by making qMin() allow mixed-type arguments and, apparently, by removing the annoying MSVC warnings that, in Qt 5, so nicely pin-pointed all these implicit conversions as hard errors.

There were several real bugs in e.g. the QBuffer code corresponding to int/qsizetype, so there's probably more.

Acceptance criterium: every {{int}} has been inspected and, if needed, ported to {{qsizetype}}. Unfortunately, relying on compiler warnings isn't enough, as explicit casts won't raise warnings, but need to be ported nonetheless.

content.text: After all researched actually code the changes.
From
to
and
So, what we want to do here is thus:

change Jenny's code-injection code so that it can read the injected code template from an external file, rather than have those template-snippets hard-coded inside Jenny. This avoids introducing direct injection-dependencies to multiple code flavors, and keeps the Jenny code reasonably simple. This first step is just about changing the current generator to produce the output it currently provides, but from external data files instead of from hard-coded data.
change the templated code so that it uses QJniObject instead of local/globalrefs.

amend the generation in case we need to abstract/parameterize some parts of it, like whether to generate any local/globalref-handling code. For plain Jenny generation, we do, but for QJniObjects introduced in step 2, we don't.

After this is done, we can look at changing the build of a Jenny-powered project, as a separate subtask. But the gist of that task is that currently, in the PoC, Jenny-generation is a separate step and the CMake project statically depends on its output, and we want to enhance that so that CMake can trigger the generation too (and handle all the dependencies correctly). This makes the build simpler, there aren't multiple steps needed, and it also makes it work out-of-the-box in Qt Creator by just opening a project and telling Creator to build it.
So, for part (1), the loading of code from external templates has the necessary enablers in place, the next step is to make the codegenerator use various templates for various parts.

Working on the parameter-replacing for source templates; this is a case-by-case operation data-wise, not all templates have the same data, working on the general algorithm that gets the tags to replace and the data to use for replacing.
The parameter-replacing will be using JTE, so we will need to integrate a template library. Otherwise it's madness.

fields.summary: Let's add a QAbstractItemModel to display JSON data

issuetype.description: Public suggestions
issuetype.name: Suggestion

content.text: It's kindof obvious that we should make it easy to display JSON data in a QTreeView or Qt Quick TreeView.
https://codereview.qt-project.org/c/qt/qtdoc/+/456602
is adding an example like that, but has to do it the hard way because we don't have library code for that.
But then again, most applications need to do something more specific, not just display
all
the data in its original form.  For XML in Qt Quick, we have XmlListModel, supporting something similar to a subset of XPath queries.  I wonder if there's a common JSON paradigm like that.
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/8481380/is-there-a-json-equivalent-of-xquery-xpath

There's a QML TableModel but not yet a TreeModel.  We know we should write one.  But maybe it's better to write a nice C++ class first, get it working with QTreeView, and try to make it available to QML in the QtQml.Models module at the same time, testing it with TreeView.  Alternatively, someone might want to process the JSON in QML/javascript first, and programmatically insert something into a TreeModel; so it would be nice if the same model can also be built up one-node-at-a-time, not only by parsing a JSON file to begin with.

We have QJsonDocument, QJsonArray and QJsonObject. A tree view could start with any of those as its root, depending whether you want to show the whole document or a subtree; so that would tend to make it a bit complicated.  If the code gets too complex to support all of those cases, then I think maybe it points to an architectural improvement that we need in the QJson classes (and others): some sort of generic QTreeNode class (name TBD) that all those can inherit from.  Then we could have a QTreeModel (TBD) that can make available any subtree (with one QTreeNode root) as a QAIM, and therefore available to all the views.

This would be a really nice addition to Qt! I have heard several times that ppl find QAIM quite complex to use, and having an easy alternative like this (that is built on top of QAIM) sounds like a good idea, especially if you just want to create a small model directly from QML.
I implemented one a few years back.
API docs:
https://jksh.github.io/QtDataTreeModels/build/API/html/class_json_tree_model.html
Internal docs:
https://jksh.github.io/QtDataTreeModels/build/Implementation/html/class_json_tree_model_node.html
Happy to donate the code to the Qt Project if you think the design is suitable!
XPath also supports JSON. As long as the data model is the same as XDM, it should “just work”:
But do we have any code for xpath?

points out that we do not support xpath queries: only a subset of the functionality.  So I was thinking that the JSON Model should support at least that much.  (Corrected the description above: I misspoke when I wrote that XLM supports xpath)
And now we have TreeModel

so from a QML perspective, the question is what other features we might like to have there, I suppose.  But I was thinking about a QAIM that can support widgets and Qt Quick equally well, when I wrote this.
We have at least two ways of handling JSON: QJsonDocument et al., and the QML JS engine.
For I/O in QML (to load JSON from a local file, web server, etc.), we have XHR (not recommended for local files), or we could do it with another one-off
source

property as is done in things like Image and TextDocument, or we could wait until we have a general QML I/O API (QTBUG-92155 which has some obstacles: I think maybe we should have a Qt Core VFS layer first).
So I guess we could still have a QAIM subclass, and then for QML it could be a subclass of that to add the
source

property and actually do file loading.  As with all the other cases, it’s some hassle to support both local and remote URLs: either you use QFile or QNetworkAccessManager, and the latter requires some boilerplate; which is why we need a VFS layer and a generic “go-get-it(URL)” API in Qt Core to make such things easier.  And then what about modifying and saving the JSON again… I don’t know how much demand there is for that, but would expect that someone would eventually ask for it.

The same story would tend to repeat if we some day wanted to support yet another serialization format, like YAML.  So maybe we should think of it as a reusable treemodel that can also load and save whatever formats we eventually support.

When it comes to flattening treemodels, we have the internal TreeToTableModel, which is not public yet, but I wonder if it should be.  Sometimes you want to see all the JSON, or a subtree (using a path-like query to pull it out); sometimes you just want to pull a list out of it and view it with a ListView or TableView.
There’s also
FWIW.  I used it once.

It's kindof obvious that we should make it easy to display JSON data in a QTreeView or Qt Quick TreeView.  [https://codereview.qt-project.org/c/qt/qtdoc/+/456602] is adding an example like that, but has to do it the hard way because we don't have library code for that.

But then again, most applications need to do something more specific, not just display _all_ the data in its original form.  For XML in Qt Quick, we have XmlListModel, supporting XPath queries.  I wonder if there's a common JSON paradigm like that.

There's a QML TableModel but not yet a TreeModel.  We know we should write one.  But maybe it's better to write a nice C++ class first, get it working with QTreeView, and try to make it available to QML in the QtQml.Models module at the same time, testing it with TreeView.  Alternatively, someone might want to process the JSON in QML/javascript first, and programmatically insert something into a TreeModel; so it would be nice if the same model can also be built up one-node-at-a-time, not only by parsing a JSON file to begin with.

We have QJsonDocument, QJsonArray and QJsonObject. A tree view could start with any of those as its root, depending whether you want to show the whole document or a subtree; so that would tend to make it a bit complicated.  If the code gets too complex to support all of those cases, then I think maybe it points to an architectural improvement that we need in the QJson classes (and others): some sort of generic QTreeNode class (name TBD) that all those can inherit from.  Then we could have a QTreeModel (TBD) that can make available any subtree (with one QTreeNode root) as a QAIM, and therefore available to all the views.

fields.summary: NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin QBSP

issuetype.description: A user story for the product
issuetype.name: User Story

content.text: To be able to demonstrate NVIDIA AI solution with Qt6 we need a QBSP for NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin boards.
create QBSP for the board
test it with Testbench
QBSP created. Boots and starts OK. Still display problem.
Work just started. It seems there is some problems with egl. Orin board uses different drivers, requires new config.
There are some problems when testing QBSP of Orin, the building is successful though.
The default startupscreen program will quit with error, with the platform integration set to "eglfs_kms_egldevices"(the default value for tegra board).
"resetSurface: Unable to connect stream
EGL Error : Could not create the egl surface: error = 0x321c"
Detailed log please see the attachment
Then I switch the platform from eglfs_kms_egldevices to eglfs_kms, here are two conditions.
Condition 1, if I remove "gbm" from the PACKAGECONFIG of qt6, the startupscreen program will crash, as it neither loaded eglfs_kms nor loaded eglfs_emu.
Detailed log is
Condition 2, if I keep "gbm", the startupscreen program will give the "Could not create surface with EGL_NATIVE_VISUAL_ID" error.
Detailed log is
However, when running the program with wayland as platform:
appcontroller /usr/bin/startupscreen -platform wayland
The weston default shell will be displayed and the startupscreen program will be displayed in a window.
I also noticed that there are some posts with similar problems.
This post mentioned create egl surface error 0x321c
https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/display-port-dp/247999
This post mentioned Could not create surface with EGL_NATIVE_VISUAL_ID
https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/eglfs-kms-could-not-create-surface/248340
And one post in our forum
https://forum.qt.io/topic/144104/egl-error-could-not-create-the-egl-surface-error-0x321c
Found another post that got display issues with KMS/GBM/DRI in AGX Orin board
https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/rendering-issue-with-gbm-kms-dri-on-jetson-agx-orin-devkit/235788/7
It was posted 6 months ago and still had no reply to it.
The user was using a simple demo from mesa and no Qt libraries involved.
Update:
I got driver errors when running the mesa demo kmscube with different drm mode, atomic mode and legacy mode.
The error looks like this:
[  472.797407] [drm:nv_drm_atomic_commit [nvidia_drm]]
ERROR
[nvidia-drm] [GPU ID 0x00020000] Flip event timeout on head 0

And it's like the error can affect next run. e.g., I first run the program with legacy mode, no error; then the atomic mode, got error; then the legacy mode, also got error; I will have to reset the OS to return normal.
The only image that uses EGL I can find now is the community distro
https://github.com/OE4T/tegra-demo-distro
I tried several branches, neither seemed to work. I submitted an issue here
https://github.com/OE4T/tegra-demo-distro/issues/260
No reply fron NVIDIA yet. Tried some other demo that worked fine. Investigating what is different in Qt SW.
Fix the display issue on egldevices platform:
Use a valid display attribute rather than a NULL pointer as parameter of eglGetPlatformDisplayEXT() to get EGLDisplay. The display attribute take the file handle of DRM device as an input.

Add a default framebuffer to eglstreams, rather than an invalid value -1. This modification takes directly from an existing patch: 0001-eglfs-add-a-default-framebuffer-to-NVIDIA-eglstreams.patch under meta-tegra/external/qt5-layer/recipes-qt/qt5/qtbase, which was used for qt5, this patch still applies on qt6.
The display is OK for both startup screen and other qt examples.
Verification with testbench is ongoing.
The fix has been fixes. Fix is in review. The original fix was from open-source. We should get the fix from the author, to submit the fix, not by us.
Still the license issue. The original author of the fix needs to contribute it also to open source Qt SW to allow TQC to use it in commercial releases.
The patch to Qt-base repo now available, so we can progrees with this. Also a fix to EGL (& GBM that we never use) backend available to test.
Have verifed the comments from dev and 6.6. braches, both work OK. To be picked up to 6.6. To be merged. To be verified again with official branch. One week to finish.
Verified on my local desktop and board. To be submitted.
Code changes have been submitted and verified, this can be closed.

content.text: User contacted us that he is building Qt for macOS and he needs to add the app store compliant flag. For this he needs to know which version of FFMPEG is safe to use.
FFMPEG version used are not mentioned in the wiki or documentation(
https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qtmultimedia-index.html#target-platform-and-backend-notes):
https://wiki.qt.io/Qt_6.5_Tools_and_Versions

The FFMPEG version used for Qt builds is not listed in this page. It is a dependency of QtMultimedia now it is the default media back-end. Can you let me know which version was used (per platform) and get this information added to this page for future releases please?
Could this be checked and added if possible.
Could someone please post in this ticket what it is right now for Qt 6.5.0? (on macOS specifically)
Hi, Qt provides only plugin  (a code from Qt side that knows how to use FFMPEG API) for using FFMPEG.
This code can be found at:
https://github.com/qt/qtmultimedia/tree/dev/src/plugins/multimedia/ffmpeg

Plugin means that its code may be included in Qt build if you provide necessary dependecies before build. It means that you must provide pre-built FFMPEG libs and link them to your apps afterwards. If no FFMPEG libs provided Qt will use other backends. So its up to you what version of FFMPEG to use.
> its up to you what version of FFMPEG to use

No it is not, we want to know what version of FFMPEG Qt developers are building against and testing against so we can reproduce that. If I used FFMPEG version 1.0 I bet it would crash (latest version is 6.0), so it is not up to the user really which version they should use.

Then use 6.0, FFMPEG API is stable, as far as I know they destroyed backward compatibility only one time, somewhere at 3 to 4 version. Anything upwards may have deprecated flags at most. I don't think Qt developers will use some old release in this situation, if you check GIT you will see that only 2 people were developing this plugin, it's better to contact them directly if you want a firm answer instead of waiting who-knows-how-long for an answer if you ever get one. Good luck!

Why can't someone just say which version is loaded up in the Qt CI system? Qt 6.5.0 builds have a cmake arg passed like this: "-DFFMPEG_DIR={{.Env.FFMPEG_DIR}}", all I want to know is what version is used. FFMPEG is the default multimedia backend.
